name: pcb-a-power
title: PCB-A POWER + I/O

finish._cont_route_planes_why: 12 September 2026: the continuation exports its own DSN, and it did so with every plane REMOVED, because finish.sh passed it no plane treatment and routeflow never put one in the finish's environment either. That makes the continuation re-route every plane pin as a wire: on C that is GND on In1, the majority of the board's connections. It is the same treatment the route itself is given in routeflow/<phase>.json, and a test holds the two in agreement.
finish._stitch_prune_why: 12 September 2026, A24, and this is the board that presented the case the tool was written for. A's route laid /PA_SLOPE and /PA_RT across In2 within 0.5 mm of the locked VBAT stitch via at (101.5, 100.5), the fill retreated by its clearance, and the via's plane end ended 0.91 mm from the nearest VBAT copper: a via connected to a 0.2 mm escape stub at one end and to nothing at the other. `check_pcb_a` refused the board for it, ONE failure of 799 checks, on a board that is 0 hard with every pair matched. Measured on a copy before it was turned on: 1 locked via removed of 621 on 38 zones, 0 left alone, hard 0 and unrouted 3 both unchanged, so nothing opened. It stays judged against the board before it (finish.sh 5b) and reverts if it opens anything.
finish._direct_close_why: 12 September 2026, A24. After the stub router had closed 9 of 10 and then 2 of 3, three connections were left and the stub router refused all three. direct_close proposed each as geometry and the DRC judged it: /CELL+ closed as a straight 9.59 mm locked track (hard 0, opens 3 to 2), and the other two were refused with what they hit named, which is the half that matters as much: /+3V3 crosses /PI_KILL and /PI_SHDN_REQ on F.Cu and meets /HEAT_EN and /EMCON_HW on both inner layers, /VBUS20 bridges the solder mask of U3 pad 2 in all five shapes. Declared for A alone: C10's eleven opens are 39 to 298 mm and this tool declines every one of them, which is the correct answer and not a reason to run it there.
finish._stub_env_why: 12 September 2026, A24, measured on a copy before it was declared. With the 0.1 mm grid and a 2.5-fold window the stub router closed 9 of 10 opens and then 0 of the last 2; with a 0.05 mm grid, a six-fold window and an 80 M node cap it closed BOTH of those two (/+3V3 with a single via, /VBUS20 with 11 tracks and a via), hard 0 throughout. The finer grid is what lets it see between the pads of U3, where /VBUS20's approach has to pass. It costs time, which is why `stub_timeout_s` exists: a cut run leaves the board as it was.
finish._rail_prune_why: 15 September 2026, A32: 0 hard, 0 unrouted, and four rails MISSED where the rail copper alone reads MET, because the router laid its own 0.5 mm inner tracks in parallel with the bands it cannot see (VIN_RAW: a 0.5 mm In2 track the whole west side beside the 6 mm B.Cu band, carrying 0.63 A at ratio 1.60). A router piece on a rail net comes off when the net stays connected without it.
finish._return_via_why: 15 September 2026, owner ruling 20:15 CEST (appendix 32.198): a ground via within 1.5 mm of every signal via, fine-pitch escape fans exempt; the finish places them after the last copper-changing stage and the board gate (intent_checks item 4) refuses a board with a signal via left without one.

_pair_order_why: 12 September 2026: A's three ribbon pairs sit on J_AB1, two of them on the header's end rows and USB_WALL on an inner row, which can only leave through the 1.14 mm channel between the columns. Laid longest-first the end-row pairs go down and their copper crosses USB_WALL's fan out of the connector, and the pass ends 2 of 3; laid with USB_WALL first it is 3 of 3. The pass is greedy and never rips up, so the pair with the least freedom goes first.
_phase_why: 12 September 2026: the phase is a fact about the board and it lived as a DEFAULT inside each generator, where gen_pcb_c.py still said C9 while the deliverable is C10, and full.sh set it for one board of six. A board's silk then names a phase `verify_deliverable` refuses, after the route, which is how A24 came to carry A18 on its front silk. `full.sh` exports this unless the caller has already set PHASE. 16 September 2026 00:15 CEST: A35 -> A36 (the route in flight is the one the set cuts; final_gate refuses a folder that is not the declared phase).
region_overflow_allow_mm_reason: A24 reads 0 hard on the placed board with NODE 1.0 mm and FES 1.4 mm outside their rectangles: both spill into free board, measured 12 September 2026. The number is the measurement plus a tenth, not a default, and it drops to zero when those two regions are sized.
_pair_env_why: 14 September 2026, measured on A's own placed board, one variable. At the tool's default corridor slack the pre-router lays 3 of 3 pairs and leaves USB_D8's two legs 1.78 mm apart, which the owner's 1 mm length gate refuses and no meander can fix: every bump the leg-length matcher proposes is refused by the leg's own map, because A's pair corridors have no free copper beside them. At 0.30 (slim 0.10) the same board lays the same 3 of 3 and **USB_D8 comes out inside the matcher's own half-millimetre tolerance**, so it never needs a bump: a wider corridor is a straighter path, and a straighter path is two legs of the same length. USB_WALL stays 1.47 mm apart at both values and is owner decision 25.
_signal_classes_why: Rule RET-001, 16 September 2026. The return-path rule asks what a net's spectral content deserves, so every signal net needs a class and a reason. A net matched by no entry here is UNKNOWN and is judged at the STRICTEST bar, so an omission costs a failure rather than buying a pass. Patterns are shell globs over the net name without its leading slash, first match wins.

_gnd_grid_why: NOT MEASURED ON THIS BOARD YET (16 September 2026). The grid is worth 90 to 109 of 130 satisfied signal vias on board E and costs board P its route, so it is a per-board measurement and not a default. Board A gets one when its current route ends and its return-via count is known.
_annular_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, annular ring rows, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): six layers at 1 oz outer: multilayer 1 oz, recommended 0.20 mm or above. The RECOMMENDED figure is taken and not the absolute minimum, because the absolute minimum is where yield starts to suffer and this board is made five at a time with no second chance before the owner has it in his hands.
